Good question — this requires identifying cardiovascular condition sets from the OMOP vocabulary, then querying the EHR. Let me take two steps in parallel: first check whether a cardiovascular concept set already exists as a cohort or vocabulary group, and second pull basic counts to understand the data.

arguments.sql_query:
-- Check if there is an existing cardiovascular-focused cohort definition we can leverage
SELECT TOP (10) 
  cohort_definition_id,
  cohort_definition_name,
  cohort_definition_syntax
FROM omop.cohort_definition
WHERE LOWER(cohort_definition_name) LIKE '%cardio%' 
   OR LOWER(cohort_definition_name) LIKE '%heart%'
   OR LOWER(cohort_definition_name) LIKE '%hypertension%'
   OR LOWER(cohort_definition_name) LIKE '%diabetes%'
ORDER BY cohort_definition_id;

-- Look at cardiovascular-relevant concept_groups in the OMOP vocabulary / concept_recommended
SELECT TOP 50
  concept_class_id,
  concept_name,
  COUNT(*) as cnt
FROM omop.concept
WHERE LOWER(concept_name) LIKE '%cardiovascular%'
   OR LOWER(concept_name) LIKE '%hypertensive disorder%'
   OR LOWER(concept_name) LIKE '%ischemic heart disease%'
   OR LOWER(concept_name) LIKE '%coronary%'
   OR LOWER(concept_name) LIKE '%heart failure%'
   OR LOWER(concept_name) LIKE '%atrial fibrillation%'
   OR LOWER(concept_name) LIKE '%congestive heart failure%'
   OR LOWER(concept_name) LIKE '%stroke%'
   OR LOWER(concept_name) LIKE '%cerebrovascular%'
   OR LOWER(concept_name) LIKE '%myocardial infarction%'
   OR LOWER(concept_name) LIKE '%angina%'
GROUP BY concept_class_id, concept_name
ORDER BY cnt DESC;

Continuing with your original question about cardiovascular multimorbidity frequency by sex: I'll build a proper analysis of cardiovascular multimorbidity using the OMOP clinical data.

arguments.sql_query:
-- Define cardiovascular disease concept set using standard concepts with specific CV-related IDs
WITH cv_conditions AS (
    SELECT DISTINCT cr.concept_id_standard as concept_id,
           cr.concept_name_standard as condition_name
    FROM omop.concept_relationship cr
    JOIN omop.concept c ON cr.concept_id_1 = c.concept_id
    WHERE c.standard_concept IN ('S', 'C')  -- standard or classification concepts
      AND c.vocabulary_id = 'Read'  -- using Read codes for clinical conditions
      AND (
          LOWER(c.concept_name) LIKE '%cardiovascular%'
          OR LOWER(c.concept_name) LIKE '%hypertensive%'
          OR LOWER(c.concept_name) LIKE '%ischemic heart disease%'
          OR LOWER(c.concept_name) LIKE '%coronary artery disease%'
          OR LOWER(c.concept_name) LIKE '%myocardial infarction%'
          OR LOWER(c.concept_name) LIKE '%angina%'
          OR LOWER(c.concept_name) LIKE '%congestive heart failure%'
          OR LOWER(c.concept_name) LIKE '%atrial fibrillation%'
          OR LOWER(c.concept_name) LIKE '%cerebrovascular%'
          OR LOWER(c.concept_name) LIKE '%stroke%'
      )
    UNION
    SELECT concept_id, concept_name FROM omop.concept 
    WHERE STANDARD_CONCEPT = 'S' AND VocabULARY_ID IN ('RxNorm', 'SNOMED')
      AND (LOWER(concept_name) LIKE '%heart failure%' OR LOWER(concept_name) LIKE '%cardiac%')
)
SELECT * FROM cv_conditions;
